trickyParts: The bash tool is a shell emulator, not bash: `$!` is empty and `wait` has no job, and `tail` is a harness builtin, so the block cannot follow a background child by pid. It holds the sequence's own file with flock before detaching (`flock "$sequence" setsid -f bash "$sequence" ...`); the detached bash inherits the lock, so `flock "$sequence" cat "$sequence.log"` blocks until it ends, race-free, with no sleep loop.

The tool's timeout kills every descendant of the call, even one in a session of its own: `setsid --wait` (child in a new session, still a descendant) was killed (its EXIT trap ran, its work did not finish). `setsid -f` forks and exits, reparenting the sequence to pid 1 (measured ppid 1), which the tool's kill no longer reaches.

Probe of the tool's kill: a python logging every 20 ms after SIGTERM logged nothing in two of my runs (as the call's command and under bash -c); the tester's probe logged 70 ms. Either way a trap that runs kubectl cannot finish.

The detached sequence prints `sequence: process <pid>; a deliberate stop is: kill -TERM -- -<pid>`; pid is also its process group since setsid made it a session leader. Its exit status is printed last as `sequence: exit <status>` because the waiting call prints output, not status.
